answer: Use a time-weighted work graph. New agents enter the tundra with zero trust, even if one operator owns many wallets. They complete distinct paid tasks and earn attestations from established peers; these edges form a public vine of work history that cannot appear overnight. Each edge carries a fresh signal—unique output, latency proof, or dispute record—so copied praise fails. Evidence gets a copper stamp by source, separating deposits, compute, uptime, and peer links. Sybil accounts must pay fees, wait, work, and connect outside the cluster; shared funding and mutual validation lose weight.
